newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Uniban approves merger with Moroccan bank.
newsitem.headline: Uniban approves merger with Moroccan bank.

text.p: Spanish Uniban bank has approved a merger with Morocco's leading Wafabank, a Uniban spokesman said on Friday.
Wafabank has paid about $28 million for 100 percent or 2,46 million shares in Uniban, a bourse official said.
"We also expect Wafabank to increase its capital by an estimated 50 million dirhams after a meeting at end March," he added.
Some minority Uniban shareholders have opposed the deal but a Casablanca-based market analyst told Reuters that Wafabank had offered them one Wafabank share in exchange for five shares of Uniban.
The minority group, which holds around 7.0 percent of Uniban stock, continues to dispute the deal before a court of Casablanca, the analyst said.
A Wafabank official earlier said the deal would be completed soon and confirmed the capital increase.
Wafabank said on Friday it made a net profit of 242 million dirhams ($25.7 million) in calendar 1996, up 20 percent on the 201 million dirhams of the previous year.
It said deposits totalled 13.8 billion dirhams, an increase of 14.25 percent over the previous period, lifting the bank's market share to 9.8 percent from nine percent.
Loans to clients rose just over 16 percent to 11.1 billion dirhams, while its mutual funds raised 997 million dirhams, 37 percent of the market.

A private Moroccan group owns 50.4 percent of Wafabank. Another 10.4 percent, previously held by French Groupe Suez, was ceded last July to Indosuez Bank group. The remaining 39.2 percent of Wafabank's equity is publicly owned.
The bank said it was paying a dividend of 13 dirhams per share for 1996 against 12 dirhams for 1995.
Uniban showed a 27.2 million dirham loss in 1995 due mainly to provisions for non-performing debt, the bank said. No updated figures for 1996 were immediately available.
The dissolution of Uniban and its delisting from the Casablanca stock market after its merger with Wafabank is expected by end of the first half 1997, a bourse spokesman said.
Wafabank showed a market capitalisation of 3.05 billion dirhams in 1996, up 51.2 percent over the previous year, the bank said. It also registered a liquidity rate of 54.1 percent in 1996, it said.
Shareholders equity rose 10 percent to 1.82 billion dirhams in 1996 compared with 1995, Wafabank added.
Wafabank and Uniban are among the 47 companies listed on the 68-year old Casablanca bourse. The two stocks were respectively traded on Friday at 725 dirhams and 140 dirhams.
